column3: **Details**
**AICTE Swanath Scholarship Scheme** (also listed as “AICTE‑Swanath Scholarship” and “AICTE Swanath Scholarship Scheme for Orphans & Defence Wards”)
All India Council for Technical Education (AICTE) in partnership with the Ministry of Education, Government of India

To provide financial assistance to the most vulnerable sections of society—orphans, children whose parents died due to COVID‑19, and wards of Armed Forces/ Central Paramilitary Forces personnel who were martyred in action—so that they can pursue technical education (engineering, technology, architecture, pharmacy, diploma, or degree programmes) without monetary hindrance.
**₹ 50,000 per academic year** (paid as a lump‑sum or in two instalments, depending on the institute’s disbursement policy).
No fixed ceiling; the scheme is open to **all eligible students** who meet the criteria and submit a complete application before the deadline.

The AICTE portal lists three overlapping deadlines for the 2026‑27 academic year. **The latest date is 3 October 2026**. (Earlier deadlines – 23 Sept 2026 and 28 Sept 2026 – are for institutions that close their internal selection earlier.)

1. **Category of beneficiaries**
• Orphans (both paternal and maternal) – i.e., a student whose both parents are deceased.
• Children whose **one or both parents died due to COVID‑19** (verified by a death certificate stating the cause of death).
• **Wards of Armed Forces or Central Paramilitary Forces personnel** who were **martyred in action** (death certificate/official service record required).

2. **Academic eligibility**
• Must be an **Indian citizen** (NRIs/OCI are not eligible).
• Enrolled (or seeking admission) in an **AICTE‑approved technical programme** – undergraduate (B.Tech/B.Arch/B.Pharm), postgraduate (M.Tech/M.Arch/M.Pharm) **or** diploma courses.
• Minimum **60 % aggregate** (or equivalent CGPA) in the most recent qualifying examination (10th, 12th, or previous semester).
• Must **not be a recipient of any other central‑government scholarship** for the same academic year (except for merit‑based scholarships that do not cover tuition).

3. **Financial eligibility**
• Family **annual income should be ≤ ₹ 4 lakhs** (as per the latest income‑tax return or BPL certificate).
• If the student belongs to a **Scheduled Caste / Scheduled Tribe / Other Backward Class**, the income ceiling is relaxed to **₹ 6 lakhs**.

1. **Application Form** – filled online on the AICTE scholarship portal (https://scholarship.aicte-india.org).
2. **Proof of Identity** – Aadhaar card, PAN card, or passport (copy).
3. **Proof of Indian Citizenship** – Birth certificate or passport.
4. **Proof of orphan/parental death** –
• Death certificate of both parents (for orphans).
• Death certificate stating COVID‑19 as cause of death (for COVID‑19 wards).
• Service record & death certificate of the defence personnel (for defence wards).
5. **Academic documents** –
• Latest mark‑sheet / grade‑card (10th, 12th, or previous semester).
• Admission/offer letter from the AICTE‑approved institute.
6. **Income proof** –
• Income‑Tax Return (ITR) of the family for the previous financial year, **or**
• BPL (Below Poverty Line) certificate issued by the State Government.
7. **Bank details** – Cancelled cheque or passbook copy showing the student’s name and account number (for direct credit of the scholarship).
8. **Passport‑size photographs** – 2 recent colour photographs (size 2 × 2 cm) with white background.
9. **Affidavit** – Self‑declaration that the information furnished is true and that the student is not receiving any other central scholarship for the same year.

1. **Register** on the AICTE scholarship portal using a valid email ID and mobile number.
2. **Create a new “Swanath Scholarship” application** and fill in personal, academic, and family‑income details.
3. **Upload all required documents** (PDF, max 2 MB each). The portal validates file format and size.
4. **Enter bank details** for direct credit.
5. **Review** the entire form, tick the declaration box, and **submit**.
6. After submission, you will receive an **application reference number (ARN)** on your registered email and SMS.
7. The **institution’s scholarship cell** verifies the documents and forwards the application to AICTE.
8. AICTE’s review committee **shortlists** candidates based on eligibility and income criteria.
9. **Final selection list** is published on the portal (usually 2‑3 weeks after the deadline).
10. **Disbursement** – The scholarship amount is transferred directly to the student’s bank account at the start of each semester (or as a single annual payment, as per the institute’s policy).

• **Opening of online portal:** 1 July 2026
• **Last date for institute‑wise internal selection:** 23 Sept 2026 (some institutes)
• **Final AICTE deadline for all applications:** **3 Oct 2026**
• **Result announcement:** Mid‑October 2026
• **First disbursement:** November 2026 (or as per institute schedule)

• **AICTE Scholarship Help‑Desk:** 1800‑425‑2026 (toll‑free)
• **Email:** scholarship@aicte-india.org
• **Website:** https://scholarship.aicte-india.org (FAQs, downloadable application guide, and sample documents)

**Q1. Can I apply if I am a defence ward but my parent died of natural causes (not in action)?**
  A. No. The scheme is only for wards of personnel **martyred in action**.

**Q2. Is the scholarship renewable for the entire course?**
  A. Yes, provided the student maintains the minimum academic performance (60 % aggregate) and continues to meet the income and category criteria each year. The institute must submit an annual renewal form.

**Q3. What if I receive a merit‑based scholarship from my college?**
  A. You can still receive the Swanath Scholarship as long as the other scholarship does **not** cover the same financial need (i.e., tuition/fees). The declaration form asks you to specify other scholarships.

**Q4. Do I need to submit a separate application for each academic year?**
  A. Yes. After the first year, the institute will ask you to fill a **renewal form** each subsequent year.

**Q5. Can a student who is a **single‑parent child** (only one parent alive) apply?**
  A. No. The scheme is strictly for **orphans** (both parents deceased) or the other two categories listed above.

• **AICTE Pragati Scholarship for Girl Students** – ₹ 50,000 / yr (deadline 23 Sept 2026).
• **AICTE Saksham Scholarship for Specially‑Abled Students** – ₹ 50,000 / yr (deadline 23 Sept 2026).
• **Post‑Graduate Scholarship (AICTE)** – ₹ 1,12,400 / month for PG technical programmes (no deadline – applied through institute).

column1: ## How to Start Right Now (Step‑by‑Step Walk‑through)
1. **Gather Documents**
- Death certificates (both parents OR COVID‑19 death certificate OR defence service death certificate).
- Latest mark‑sheet (12th or previous semester).
- Income‑Tax Return or BPL certificate.
- Aadhaar & bank passbook.
2. **Create an Account**
- Go to **https://scholarship.aicte-india.org**.
- Click **“New User – Register”**, enter your email, mobile, and set a password.
3. **Start a New Application**
- After login, select **“Apply for AICTE Swanath Scholarship”**.
- Choose the **category** (Orphan / COVID‑19 Ward / Defence Ward).
4. **Enter Details**
- Fill personal info, academic scores, family income, and upload the scanned PDFs.
5. **Bank Details**
- Enter **IFSC code, account number, account holder name** exactly as shown on the passbook.
6. **Review & Submit**
- Double‑check every field.
- Tick the **“I hereby declare that the information furnished is true and correct”** box.
- Click **“Submit”.**
7. **Save Confirmation**
- Screenshot or download the **“Application Acknowledgement”** (contains ARN).
8. **Follow Up**
- Email or call your college’s scholarship cell to confirm receipt.
- Keep an eye on the portal for status updates (e.g., “Under Review”, “Shortlisted”, “Awarded”).

**13 September 2026** (online portal closes on this date; late submissions are not accepted).

4. **Submit the application** and note the **Application Reference Number (ARN)**.
5. The institute’s **Scholarship Coordinator** verifies the data and forwards it to AICTE.
6. AICTE reviews and **issues the sanction letter** (usually within 2–3 weeks).
7. The scholarship amount is **directly credited** to the student’s bank account (or to the institute’s fee‑collection account, which then adjusts the fee).

Maulana Azad National Fellowship (M.A.N.F.) – also listed as “Maulana Azad National Fellowship for Minority Students”
Ministry of Minority Affairs, Government of India (in partnership with the University Grants Commission – UGC)

To provide financial assistance to students belonging to minority communities (Muslim, Christian, Sikh, Buddhist, Jain, Zoroastrian/Parsi) for pursuing **M.Phil.** and **Ph.D.** programmes at UGC‑recognised universities/institutes.

**₹ 35,000 per year** (i.e., ₹ 2,916.67 per month).
*Note:* The amount is fixed for the entire tenure of the fellowship (normally 2 years for M.Phil. and 5 years for Ph.D.).

1. **Community** – Must belong to one of the recognized minority communities (Muslim, Christian, Sikh, Buddhist, Jain, Zoroastrian/Parsi).
2. **Academic Qualification** –
• For **M.Phil.**: Minimum 55 % aggregate (or equivalent CGPA) in a relevant Master’s degree.
• For **Ph.D.**: Minimum 55 % aggregate (or equivalent CGPA) in a relevant Master’s degree **or** a valid UGC‑NET/CSIR‑NET/SET qualification.
3. **Admission** – Must have secured admission (or be in the process of admission) to a **UGC‑recognised** university/institute for the intended M.Phil./Ph.D. programme.
4. **Age** – No upper age limit, but the candidate must be a **full‑time** student throughout the fellowship period.
**8 October 2026** (online portal closes at 23:59 IST). The deadline is **strict**; late submissions are not entertained.

1. **Register** on the Ministry of Minority Affairs’ scholarship portal (https://scholarships.gov.in).
2. **Create a new application** and select “Maulana Azad National Fellowship for Minority Students”.
3. **Fill in personal & academic details** (including community certificate, academic transcripts, admission letter, etc.).
4. **Upload required documents** (see “Documents Required” below).
5. **Pay the nominal processing fee** (if any; usually waived for this fellowship).
6. **Submit** the application and note the **Application Reference Number**.
7. **Track** the status on the portal; you may be called for document verification or interview.

• **Community Certificate** (issued by a competent authority, e.g., State Minority Commission).
• **Proof of Indian Citizenship** (Aadhaar card, passport, or voter ID).
• **Academic Documents** – Mark sheets & certificates of the qualifying degree(s) (Bachelor’s & Master’s).
• **UGC‑NET/CSIR‑NET/SET Scorecard** (if applying for Ph.D. and you have it).
• **Admission Letter/Provisional Admission Letter** from the university for the M.Phil./Ph.D. programme.
• **Curriculum Vitae** (including publications, conferences, research experience).
• **Research Proposal** (maximum 2,000 words) outlining the intended research work.
• **Bank Account Details** (passbook or cancelled cheque) for direct transfer of the stipend.
• **Passport‑size Photograph** (recent, white background, 3.5 × 4.5 cm).

• The stipend of **₹ 35,000 per year** is transferred **quarterly** (i.e., every 3 months) directly to the bank account provided.
• The amount is **tax‑exempt** under Section 10(17A) of the Income Tax Act, provided the recipient is a full‑time student.

• For **M.Phil.** (2‑year tenure) – the fellowship is automatically continued for the second year, provided the student maintains **minimum 55 %** aggregate in the first year and submits a progress report.
• For **Ph.D.** (5‑year tenure) – renewal is required **annually**. The student must submit a **progress report**, **annual academic transcript**, and **affidavit of continued full‑time status**.

• The fellowship **does not cover tuition fees**; it is a pure stipend.
• The fellowship is **non‑transferable** and **non‑cumulative** with other central fellowships (e.g., UGC‑JRF). If you receive another central fellowship, you must surrender one of them.
• Failure to submit progress reports or maintain the required academic standing may lead to **termination** of the fellowship.

• **Phone:** 011‑2301 5555 (Monday‑Friday, 10 am‑5 pm IST)
• **Website:** https://scholarships.gov.in (FAQs, downloadable application form, and detailed guidelines)

column3: **Details**
Department of Science & Technology (DST), Government of India

To attract and retain talented Indian students in basic & natural sciences (Physics, Chemistry, Mathematics, Biology, etc.) for higher‑education programmes (B.Sc./M.Sc./Integrated M.Sc., M.Tech, M.Phil, Ph.D.).
**₹ 80,000 per annum** (disbursed in 4 equal instalments of ₹ 20,000 each). The amount is **tax‑exempt** and **non‑recoverable**.

1. **Research Exposure** – Access to DST‑funded research projects, labs, and national research facilities (e.g., NISER, IISc, CSIR labs).
2. **Mentorship** – Each scholar is assigned a senior scientist/ faculty mentor who guides the research work and career planning.
3. **Conference & Travel Support** – Up to **₹ 5,000** per year (subject to availability) for attending national/international conferences, workshops, or seminars related to the scholar’s research area.
4. **Networking** – Membership in the **INSPIRE Community** (online portal, annual meet‑ups, webinars) where scholars can interact with peers, senior scientists, and industry experts.
5. **Priority for Further Funding** – Scholars are given preference when applying for other DST schemes (e.g., INSPIRE‑Fellowship, DST‑SERB grants).
6. **Recognition** – Certificate of Merit and a mention on the DST website, which adds weight to CVs and graduate‑school applications.

- **Indian citizen** (by birth or naturalisation).
- **Age limit:** ≤ 30 years on the first day of the academic session (relaxed to 35 years for candidates with a disability).
- **Academic qualification:**
• For **B.Sc./M.Sc./Integrated M.Sc.** – Must have secured **≥ 75 %** (or **≥ 70 %** for SC/ST/PwD) in the preceding qualifying exam (12th class for B.Sc., B.Sc. for M.Sc.).
• For **M.Tech/M.Phil/Ph.D.** – Must have secured **≥ 75 %** (or **≥ 70 %** for SC/ST/PwD) in the preceding degree (B.Tech/M.Sc. for M.Tech, M.Sc. for M.Phil, etc.).
- **Merit:** Must be among the **top 1 %** of the All‑India Rank (AIR) in the **JEE‑Advanced**, **NEET‑UG**, **JEE‑Main**, **KVPY**, **NEST**, **JEST**, **GATE**, or any other nationally recognised entrance exam in the relevant discipline.
- **No other full‑time scholarship** (government or private) covering the same period may be received simultaneously.
**7 November 2026** (midnight IST). The portal closes on this date; late submissions are not entertained.

1. **Register** on the DST INSPIRE portal: (create a user ID & password).
2. **Fill in the online application form** – personal details, academic records, entrance‑exam scores, and upload required documents (see table below).
3. **Upload a recent passport‑size photograph** (JPEG, ≤ 200 KB) and **signature** (JPEG, ≤ 200 KB).
4. **Select the desired programme** (B.Sc., M.Sc., Integrated M.Sc., M.Tech, M.Phil, Ph.D.) and the **institution** where you will enrol.
5. **Submit** the form and note the **Application Reference Number (ARN)**.
6. **Print** the acknowledgment receipt and keep it for future reference.

• **Scanned copy of Class 12 / Graduation / Post‑Graduation mark‑sheet** (original + certified copy).
• **Scanned copy of the qualifying entrance‑exam scorecard** (JEE‑Advanced, JEE‑Main, NEET‑UG, KVPY, NEST, JEST, GATE, etc.).
• **Proof of Indian citizenship** (Passport, Aadhaar, or Birth Certificate).
• **Passport‑size photograph** (white background, 3.5 cm × 4.5 cm).
• **Signature image** (black ink on white paper).
• **Letter of admission / provisional admission** from the university/college (if already obtained).
• **Bank account details** (IFSC, account number, account holder name) for scholarship disbursement.
• **Self‑declaration** (PDF) stating that the applicant is not receiving any other full‑time scholarship for the same period.

1. **Eligibility verification** – DST checks academic & entrance‑exam criteria.
2. **Merit ranking** – Candidates are ranked based on entrance‑exam percentile and academic performance.
3. **Short‑list** – Top‑ranked candidates (usually 500–800 per year) are shortlisted.
4. **Final award** – Selected scholars receive an **award letter** (PDF) with bank‑account details for the first instalment.

- **First instalment** (₹ 20,000) – within 30 days of award letter.
- **Subsequent instalments** – after submission of **mid‑term progress report** (usually after 6 months) and **annual academic transcript**.
- **Final instalment** – after submission of **final year/Ph.D. completion certificate**.

- **Mid‑term progress report** (research work, coursework, any publications).
- **Annual academic transcript** (marks, attendance).
- **Final completion report** (thesis abstract, list of publications/patents, if any).
- All reports must be uploaded on the INSPIRE portal; failure to submit on time may lead to **suspension or recovery** of the scholarship.

column3: Yes. You may receive **only one central post‑matric scholarship** (the highest amount will be paid), but you can also apply for **state‑level** scholarships **in addition** (e.g., a state‑government SC scholarship).

column2: **What if my family income is slightly above the ceiling?**
column3: Some states (e.g., Maharashtra, Karnataka) have a **higher ceiling (₹ 3 Lakh)**. Check the **state scholarship portal** for those states. If you are above the central limit, you may still qualify for **state‑specific** schemes.

column2: **What if I change my college or course mid‑year?**
column3: You must **inform the scholarship authority** within 15 days and upload the **new admission letter**. Failure to do so may lead to suspension of the scholarship.

column2: **How long does the approval process take?**
column3: Typically **15‑30 days** after submission, provided all documents are clear. Delays usually happen due to mismatched names or illegible scans.

column2: **What if I am a **dual‑category** (e.g., SC & OBC)?**
column3: The **SC/ST** category is **higher** in the reservation hierarchy, so you should apply under **SC/ST**. The scholarship amount will be the same.

column2: **Can I apply if I am studying abroad?**
column3: The central post‑matric scholarships are **only for courses in India** (recognised by the UGC/AICTE). For overseas studies, look for **MHRD’s “Study Abroad Scholarship”** (different eligibility).

#### 3. Application Procedure – Step‑by‑Step (with screenshots description)
1. **Create an account** on the AICTE portal using your mobile number linked to Aadhaar.
- *Screen 1*: “New User? Register Here”.
- Fill name, email, mobile, and set a strong password (minimum 8 characters, mix of letters, numbers, symbols).
2. **Verify OTP** sent to your mobile and **activate** the account.
3. **Log in** → **Dashboard** → **Apply for Scholarships** → **Select “Pragati – Girl Technical Degree”** (or “Diploma”).
4. **Fill Personal Details** – they are auto‑populated from Aadhaar (name, DOB, address). Verify and edit if needed.
5. **Academic Details** – enter:
- Institute name, AICTE approval number (found on the institute’s website or admission letter).
- Programme name, start year, current semester, CGPA/percentage.
6. **Financial Details** – upload the latest **ITR** or **Form 16** of the parent/guardian. If you have a **self‑employed** parent, attach the **Income Tax Assessment Order**.
7. **Upload Documents** – use the **“Browse”** button for each required file. The portal shows a **green tick** when the upload succeeds.
8. **Review & Submit** – the portal will display a **summary page**. Click **“Submit Application”** only after double‑checking every entry.
9. **Confirmation** – you will receive an **SMS** and **email** with an **Application Reference Number (ARN)**. Save this ARN; you’ll need it for any future queries.

10. **Post‑submission** – the portal may ask for **additional verification** (e.g., a scanned copy of the **college‑issued “No Backlog” letter**). Upload within the **7‑day** window to avoid disqualification.

11. **Result** – the scholarship committee releases the list of **selected candidates** on the portal (usually 2‑3 weeks after the deadline). If selected, the amount is credited directly to the **bank account** linked to your Aadhaar.

column1: #### 5. After You Receive the Scholarship

1. **Bank Account Linking** – The amount is transferred to the **bank account** linked with your Aadhaar. If you don’t have one, open a **Zero‑Balance Savings Account** (e.g., SBI, Axis, HDFC) and **link** it via the **Aadhaar‑eKYC** process.
2. **Utilisation** – The funds are **restricted** to:
- Tuition fees (up to 70 % of the total amount)
- Books & stationery (up to 20 %)
- Incidentals (travel, internet, etc.) – remaining 10 %

3. **Reporting** – You must submit a **mid‑year academic progress report** (CGPA/percentage) and a **final year completion certificate** to the portal. Failure to do so may lead to **recovery of the amount**.

column1: ### Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs)

column3: Answer

column2: **Can I apply for more than one minority scholarship at the same time?**
column3: **Yes.** Most schemes are **cumulative** as long as you meet each scheme’s eligibility. However, some scholarships (especially those covering the same expense, e.g., tuition) may have a “no‑double‑benefit” clause. Always read the “Exclusions” section of each notification.

column2: **Do I need a separate bank account for each scholarship?**
column3: **No.** All government scholarships are transferred directly to the **Aadhaar‑linked bank account** you provide. You can use the same account for multiple scholarships.

column2: **What if I miss the deadline for the Merit‑cum‑Means scholarship?**
column3: The scheme is **annual**; the next intake will be announced for **2027** (usually around **June‑July**). Meanwhile, you can apply for other rolling‑type scholarships (Post‑Matric, Central Sector, etc.).

column2: **I belong to a minority community but my family income is above the limit. Are there any scholarships for me?**
column3: Yes. Some scholarships (e.g., **Chief Minister’s Overseas Scholarship**, **institution‑specific merit scholarships**) **do not have an income ceiling** or have a higher ceiling (₹ 8‑10 L). Look for “Merit‑based” rather than “Means‑based” schemes.

column2: **Do I need to re‑apply every year for the Merit‑cum‑Means scholarship?**
column3: **Yes.** The scholarship is **renewable** each academic year. You must submit a **renewal application** before the start of the next semester, providing the latest marksheet and income proof.

column2: **My community certificate is in a regional language. Will it be accepted?**
column3: Most central‑government portals accept **English or Hindi** PDFs. If your certificate is in a regional language, **attach a notarised English translation** along with the original.

column2: **What if I have a disability in addition to being from a minority community?**
column3: You can **simultaneously apply** for **disability‑specific scholarships** (e.g., *National Handicapped Scholarship Scheme*) **and** minority scholarships. Both benefits can be combined unless explicitly prohibited.

column3: Details

**National Means‑cum‑Merits Scholarship (NMMS)** – a centrally‑funded programme of the Ministry of Education (formerly HRD) aimed at encouraging meritorious students from economically‑weaker sections (EWS) to continue their studies beyond Class 8.

• Students who have **passed Class 8** and are now enrolled in **Class 9** (or Class 10).
• Belong to **economically‑weaker families** (annual household income ≤ ₹ 1.5 lakh).
• Have **good academic performance** – usually the top 20 % of the class (or a minimum of 60 % aggregate marks in Class 8).

• Prevent drop‑out after Class 8.
• Provide a financial incentive so that students can focus on studies rather than work.
• Recognise and reward academic merit combined with economic need.

**₹ 12,000 per year** (disbursed in two equal instalments of ₹ 6,000 each).

1. **Academic criteria**
• Passed Class 8 in the previous academic year.
• Secured **≥ 60 %** aggregate (or be in the top 20 % of the class, whichever is higher).
• No history of disciplinary action.
2. **Economic criteria**
• Annual family income **≤ ₹ 1.5 lakh** (as per the latest income certificate).
• Belongs to **EWS/EBC/SC/ST/OBC‑non‑creamy‑layer** categories (the scheme is open to all categories, but the income ceiling is the key factor).
3. **Age**
• No upper age limit, but the student must be **currently studying in Class 9** (or Class 10).
4. **Other conditions**
• Must be a **resident of the state/UT** where the application is submitted.
• Must **not be receiving any other scholarship** for the same academic year (except for scholarships that are not overlapping, e.g., sports scholarships).

column3: Yes, **provided the other scholarship is not for the same purpose** (i.e., not a merit‑cum‑means scholarship). Over‑lapping scholarships for different purposes (e.g., sports, cultural) are allowed.

column2: **2. What if my family income is slightly above ₹ 1.5 lakh?**
column3: Some states relax the ceiling to **₹ 2 lakh** for families with **two or more children** in school. Check your state portal for exact limits.

column2: **3. I missed the 7 Nov deadline – can I still apply?**
column3: Occasionally, states issue a **late‑submission window** (usually 2‑3 weeks) for genuine cases. Contact the **State Scholarship Cell** immediately with a justification letter.

column2: **4. How is the scholarship amount disbursed?**
column3: Direct **Electronic Funds Transfer (EFT)** to the bank account you entered. No cheque or cash hand‑over.

column2: **5. What if I change schools in Class 9?**
column3: You must inform the **previous school** to close the application and the **new school** to re‑verify your details. The scholarship can continue as long as you remain in the same academic year.

column2: **6. Do I need to re‑apply for Class 10?**

ScienceResearchSocial ScienceSRFDetailsICMR-Junior Research Fellowship (ICMR-JRF) examination is the first step in the process of admission to the PhD/Research Programme through the council's support. ICMR holds a national-level examination for determining the
eligibility of Indian National candidates for the award of Junior Research Fellowships (JRF) through the Indian Council of Medical
Research. The award of Junior Research Fellowship to the successful eligible candidates will depend on their finding placement in a medical college/hospital/university / national laboratory/institution of higher learning and research as applicable. The award of JRF is
made on a merit basis by holding an entrance examination after issuing a countrywide admission notice.Scheme of Test:The test will consist of one paper of 2 hours duration.The paper will consist of 2 Sections. The Aptitude Section (Section A) will have 50 questions on
(i) scientific phenomenon in everyday life; (ii) general knowledge in sciences; and (iii) common statistics. All these questions would be compulsory with each question carrying 1 mark. The subject Specific Section (Section B & C) would pertain to (B) Life Sciences and (C)
Social Science. The candidate may attempt questions in either of the two areas. Each area of section B & C would have 100 questions and the candidate may attempt any 75 questions in the predesigned area of Section B or C. Candidates are required to indicate the option
for Section B or C in the application form too.Each question carries one mark. Negative marking @ 0.25 will be made for each of the wrong answers. The questions in both sections would appear in English only.The final result will be based on an aggregate of 55 %
marks obtained in both the sections for the General category and OBC and 50% for SC/ST and physically handicapped.The test will be held in the following streams:Aptitude test (common for all) (2) Life Sciences (3) Social Sciences.Subjects covered under Life Sciences
include microbiology, physiology, molecular biology, genetics, human nutrition, human biology, biotechnology, biochemistry, biophysics, immunology, pharmacology, zoology, environmental sciences, botany, public health veterinary science, and bioinformatics.
Subjects covered under Social Sciences include psychology, sociology, home sciences, statistics, anthropology, social work, and health economics.A total of 150 Fellowships would be awarded. 120 Fellowships would be awarded for work in the field of biomedical sciences
with emphasis on Life Sciences (like microbiology, physiology, molecular biology, genetics, human biology, bioinformatics, biotechnology, biochemistry, biophysics, immunology, Pharmacology, zoology, environmental science, botany, veterinary sciences, bio-
informatics, etc.). Thirty Fellowships would be awarded for work with an emphasis on Social sciences like psychology, sociology, home science, statistics, anthropology, social work, and Health Economics.Two separate merit lists, one comprising the candidates qualifying
for life sciences and the second for those candidates qualifying for social sciences, will be made on the basis of their performance in the above test.The candidates selected for the JRF programme of ICMR would be permitted to enroll themselves in the Ph.D. programme of
any University recognised by the UGC/MCI. However, the JRF programme would not have any connection with the Ph.D. programme.
The validity of the fellowship awarded to a candidate will be six months.Another 100 candidates would be selected for consideration for positions of JRF under various research schemes of ICMR (subject to fulfilling the conditions for appointment under the schemes) for
the duration of that scheme. These JRFs would also be permitted to complete a Ph.D. while working in the scheme if enrolled. The validity of the result will be two years for placement in ICMR-funded projects.SC/ST/OBC/Physically handicapped (PH) applicants will

ICMR.BenefitsThe Junior Research fellows will be paid a monthly stipend of â‚131,000/- for the 1st & 2nd year.The Senior Research

To develop a pool of highly‑qualified Indian researchers by providing **advanced training and research exposure** at world‑class agricultural institutions abroad. The fellowship aims to bring back cutting‑edge knowledge, technologies and networks that can be applied to Indian agriculture.

• Indian nationals (citizens of India)
• Graduates (M.Sc./M.Tech) or post‑graduates (Ph.D.) in **agricultural sciences, allied sciences, biotechnology, food technology, horticulture, animal husbandry, fisheries, soil science, agronomy, plant breeding, agricultural engineering, etc.**
• Candidates who have **secured at least 55 %** (or equivalent CGPA) in the qualifying degree.

1. **M.Sc./M.Tech** (or equivalent) in a relevant discipline with a minimum of **55 %** marks (or 6.0 CGPA on a 10‑point scale).
2. **Ph.D.** candidates (full‑time) who have completed **at least 2 years** of research and have a **minimum of 55 %** in the qualifying degree.

Below is a **complete, step‑by‑step guide** that covers everything you need to know – from the purpose of the scheme to eligibility, benefits, how to apply, required documents, and useful tips.
### 1️⃣  What is the Central Sector Scheme of Scholarships?

column3: Details

To provide **financial assistance** to meritorious and/or economically‑disadvantaged students pursuing **under‑graduate, postgraduate, diploma, and professional courses** in recognized colleges and universities across India.
100 % central‑government funded (no contribution from state governments or institutions).
Ministry of Education (formerly Ministry of Human Resource Development) in partnership with the **National Scholarship Portal (NSP)** and the **College/University Scholarship Cell**.

• General‑merit students (e.g., National Merit Scholarship).
• Reserved‑category students (SC, ST, OBC‑NCL, PWD).
• Minority‑community students (e.g., Maulana Azad National Scholarship).
• Students from economically weaker sections (EWS).
• Specific‑need scholarships (e.g., for girl students, sports, research).

• Tuition fees (full or partial).
• Maintenance allowance (stipend for living expenses).
• Books, equipment, and other academic expenses (depending on the specific sub‑scheme).

column2: **Typical Amounts** *(varies by sub‑scheme; figures shown for reference only)*

• **Merit‑based**: ₹10,000‑₹30,000 per annum.

• **Research/Ph.D.**: ₹15,000‑₹25,000 per month (stipend).
Usually **one academic year** (renewable on meeting performance criteria).

**No fixed national deadline** – each academic year the portal opens a **“Scholarship Application Window”** (typically June‑July for the upcoming year). Individual colleges may have internal cut‑off dates, so check both NSP and your institution’s scholarship cell.

### 3️⃣  Eligibility – General Checklist (applies to most central‑sector scholarships)
1. **Citizenship** – Indian citizen (or NRI/OCI with a valid Indian passport for certain schemes).
2. **Admission** – Enrolled in a **recognised college/university** (UG, PG, Diploma, Professional, or Research).
3. **Academic Performance** – Minimum percentage/CGPA as specified (usually 60 %–75 %).
4. **Income Limit** – Family annual income **≤ ₹2 lakhs** (SC/ST), **≤ ₹4 lakhs** (OBC‑NCL/EWS), or **no limit** for merit‑based schemes.
5. **No Pending Dues** – No outstanding fees, library dues, or disciplinary actions in the current institution.
6. **Certificates** – Valid caste/tribe/minority/EWS certificate (if applicable) issued by a competent authority.
7. **Age** – Some scholarships (e.g., research fellowships) have an upper age limit (usually 30‑35 years for UG/PG, 35‑40 years for Ph.D.).

### 5️⃣  How to Apply – Step‑by‑Step (Using the National Scholarship Portal)
1. **Create an Account**
- Go to **https://scholarships.gov.in**.
- Click **“New User Registration”** → Fill in name, email, mobile number, and create a password.
- Verify OTP sent to your mobile/email.
2. **Complete Your Profile**
- Add **Aadhaar**, **PAN**, and **bank account** details.
- Upload **passport‑size photo** and **signature** (both in JPEG/PNG, ≤ 200 KB).
3. **Select the Scholarship**
- In the dashboard, click **“Apply for Scholarship”** → Choose **“Central Sector Scheme – College/University”** → Pick the specific sub‑scheme (e.g., “Post‑Matric SC Scholarship”).
4. **Enter Academic & Personal Details**
- Fill in **family income**, **caste/minority/EWS status**, **course details**, **college/university name & code**, **year of study**, etc.
5. **Upload Required Documents**
- Follow the table in Section 4. Ensure each file is **clear, legible, and within size limits**.
6. **Self‑Declaration & Submit**
- Read the declaration carefully, tick the box, and click **“Submit Application”**.
7. **Print & Save Acknowledgement**
- After submission, an **Acknowledgement Slip (PDF)** is generated. **Download & print** it – you may need to submit a hard copy to your college’s scholarship cell.
8. **College/University Verification**
- Your institution’s scholarship officer will verify the documents and **approve** the application on the portal (usually within 7‑10 working days).
9. **Final Approval & Disbursement**
- Once approved, the **scholarship amount** is transferred directly to the bank account you provided (usually at the start of each semester).
10. **Renewal (if applicable)**
- For multi‑year courses, you must **re‑apply each academic year** with updated marksheets and income proof before the renewal window opens (generally **April‑May**).
### 6️⃣  Common FAQs

column3: Answer

column2: **Do I need to have an Aadhaar to apply?**
column3: Yes. Aadhaar is mandatory for identity verification and for direct bank transfer of the scholarship amount.

column2: **What if my family income exceeds the limit?**
column3: You may still be eligible for **merit‑based** central scholarships (e.g., National Merit Scholarship) which have **no income ceiling**.

column2: **Can I apply for more than one central‑sector scholarship at a time?**
column3: **No.** You can receive **only one central‑sector scholarship** per academic year. Choose the one that offers the highest benefit.

column2: **What if I change my college or course mid‑year?**
column3: You must inform the **college scholarship cell** and update the details on NSP within **15 days**; otherwise the scholarship may be discontinued.

column2: **How long does the verification process take?**
column3: Typically **7‑15 working days** after submission, but it can be longer during peak periods.
Scholarship amounts **exempt** from income tax **provided** they are used for **educational purposes** (tuition, fees, books, etc.).

column2: **What if I have a pending library fine?**
column3: Any **pending dues** (fees, library, hostel) will **disqualify** you until cleared. Pay them first, then re‑apply.

column2: **Can I receive the scholarship if I am studying abroad?**
column3: Central‑sector scholarships are **only for Indian institutions** recognized by the UGC/AICTE. For overseas studies, look for **MHRD’s “Study Abroad” scholarships** (e.g., ICCR, IIE).

column3: Answer

column2: **Do I need to be a resident of a particular state for INSPIRE?**
column3: No. INSPIRE is a **central government** scheme; any Indian citizen can apply.

column2: **Can I apply for more than one scholarship at the same time?**
column3: Yes, **provided the total stipend does not exceed the permissible limit** set by the funding agency (usually ₹1.5 Lakh per month for Ph.D.). You must disclose any other awards in the application.

column2: **What if I change my research supervisor after getting the scholarship?**
column3: You must inform the **scholarship authority** (via the portal) and get a **new endorsement** from the new supervisor. The award may be re‑validated.

column2: **Is there a service tax or any deduction from the stipend?**
column3: The stipend is **tax‑exempt** under Section 10(17A) of the Income Tax Act, provided you are a full‑time researcher and the amount does not exceed the prescribed limit.

column2: **What happens if I discontinue my research?**
column3: The scholarship will be **withdrawn** and you may be required to **return the unspent amount**. Some schemes allow a **grace period** (usually 1 month) to submit a final report.

column2: **Can I use the stipend for travel to conferences?**
column3: Yes, most schemes allow **research‑related travel** (conference, field work) but you must submit a **travel claim** with receipts to the university’s finance office.

column2: **How long does the selection process take?**
column3: Typically **2–3 months** after the application deadline, but it can vary (especially for DST‑INSPIRE where the host institute’s verification adds extra time).

column1: ### How to Prepare & Submit the Documents

column3: Action
Collect every original document listed above.
column4: Keep a **folder** for each category (ID, academic, income, etc.) so you don’t miss anything.

column3: Scan each document at **300 dpi** in **PDF** (or JPEG for photos).
Most portals allow **≤ 2 MB** per file.
column4: If a file is too large, compress it using free tools like **ILovePDF** or **Smallpdf**.

column3: Go to the official AICTE/Ministry of Education portal (or your state’s scholarship portal).
column4: Double‑check every field; a single typo can cause rejection.

column3: Follow the order shown on the portal (usually “Identity → Academic → Income → Bank”).
column4: Use the **preview** button to ensure the uploaded file is legible.

column3: Some states charge a **₹100‑₹200** processing fee.
column4: Keep the receipt screenshot; you may need to upload it.

column3: After submission you’ll receive a **reference number**.
column4: Save this ID in a spreadsheet or note‑taking app; you’ll need it for tracking.

column3: Even though the process is online, keep **printed copies** of everything.
column4: In case the scholarship committee asks for physical verification, you’ll be ready.

column3: Check the portal or your registered email for status updates.
column4: If you receive a **“document missing”** notice, upload the required file within the stipulated time (usually 7 days).

column3: Once approved, you’ll receive a **scholarship award letter** and bank details for the first disbursement.
column4: Sign the award letter (if required) and send it back via the portal or email.

column1: ## Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs) about Documents

column3: Answer

column2: **Do I need to submit the original documents?**
column3: No. **Scanned copies** are sufficient for the online portal. Keep the originals safe for any later verification.

column2: **What if I don’t have a caste certificate?**
column3: If you belong to a **General/EWS** category, you can skip the caste certificate. For SC/ST/OBC‑Non‑Creamy, you must obtain it from the **District Collector’s office** before applying.

column2: **Can I use a school‑issued ID instead of Aadhaar?**
column3: Most portals accept **any government‑issued photo ID** (Aadhaar, Passport, Voter ID). Choose the one that is most recent and clearly readable.

column2: **My family income is just above ₹4 lakhs – can I still apply?**
column3: The **Pragati Scholarship** is primarily for economically weaker sections, but some states have a **“Merit + Need”** component. Check your state’s specific guidelines; you may still be eligible under the merit part.

column2: **I’m a diploma student; do I need a separate fee receipt?**
column3: Yes. For the **Technical Diploma** scheme, upload the **detailed fee breakup** and the **latest receipt** (even if you have paid only the first instalment).

column2: **Do I need a separate photograph for each document?**
column3: No. One **digital passport‑size photo** (JPEG, ≤ 100 KB) is usually enough for the entire application.

column2: **What if my college is not AICTE‑approved?**
column3: The scholarship is **only for AICTE‑approved programmes**. You will need to verify your college’s approval status on the AICTE website before applying.

column2: **Is a self‑declaration enough for income proof?**
column3: Some states accept a **self‑declaration** plus a **bank statement**. Others require an **official Income Certificate** from the Tehsildar. Check the specific state portal for the exact requirement.

column2: **Can I submit documents in a language other than English?**
column3: All documents must be in **English or Hindi**. If your original certificates are in another language (e.g., Tamil, Malayalam), attach a **certified translation**.

The Pragati Scholarship for Girl Students (both degree & diploma) has a **hard deadline of 13 September 2026**. Late submissions are **not accepted**. Plan to upload at least 2‑3 days before the deadline.

column3: **Details**
**Devnarayan Post‑Matric Scholarship**
Government of Rajasthan – Department of Higher Education & State Scholarship Cell
Students belonging to the **Banjara, Bairwa, Balai, Bhatia** and other **specified backward class (SBC)** communities.
**Post‑matriculation** (any course after Class 10 – i.e., 11th & 12th, diploma, undergraduate, postgraduate, professional & vocational courses).
**₹ 25,000 per academic year** (renewable each year subject to eligibility & academic performance).
**28 September 2026** (midnight IST). Applications received after this date will be rejected.
State‑government budget (Rajasthan) – no repayment required.
Varies each year; the scheme is **need‑based** and limited to eligible SBC students who meet the academic & income criteria.

column1: ### 1️⃣ Eligibility Criteria – Full Checklist

column3: **What You Need to Satisfy**
Belong to **Banjara, Bairwa, Balai, Bhatia** or any other **SBC** listed in the Rajasthan SBC list (the official list is available on the Rajasthan Scholarship Portal).
Permanent resident of **Rajasthan** (as per domicile certificate).
Enrolled in a **recognised** institution for any **post‑matric** course (11‑12, diploma, UG, PG, professional, or vocational).
Must have **secured admission** (admission letter/offer letter) for the current academic year.
Minimum **50 % aggregate** in the previous qualifying exam (e.g., 10th, 12th, diploma, UG). Some courses (professional) may require a higher cut‑off (e.g., 55 %).
**Annual family income ≤ ₹ 4 lakhs** (as per the latest income certificate). The exact ceiling may be revised each year; check the portal for the current figure.
No upper age limit for post‑matric courses, but the applicant must be **under 30 years** for professional courses (e.g., MBBS, B.Tech) as per the latest guidelines.

Cannot be a **full‑time recipient** of any other central/state post‑matric scholarship for the same course/year. Partial scholarships are allowed if the total amount does not exceed the Devnarayan award.
Indian citizen (or OCI/NRI with a valid OCI card and Rajasthan domicile).

column1: > **Tip:** Keep a copy of the **SBC community list** (PDF) from the Rajasthan Scholarship website to prove your community if asked.
### 2️⃣ Benefits & Disbursement

column3: **Details**
₹ 25,000 per year, **directly transferred** to the applicant’s bank account (or to the parent/guardian’s account if the student is a minor).
Scholarship can be **renewed each year** up to the completion of the course, provided the student continues to meet the eligibility (income, academic performance, community).
Usually **disbursed in two installments** – 1st installment after verification of admission, 2nd installment after the mid‑term results. Exact dates are announced on the portal each year.
Some years the state also provides **one‑time travel allowance** (₹ 2,000) for students moving to a different district for studies. Check the current year’s notification.

column1: ### 3️⃣ Application Procedure – Step‑by‑Step

column3: **Action**

column2: **1. Register on the Rajasthan Scholarship Portal**
column3: Go to **[scholarship.rajasthan.gov.in](https://scholarship.rajasthan.gov.in)** and click **“New User – Register”.**
column4: Use a **valid email** and **mobile number**. You will receive an OTP for verification.

column3: Fill in personal details (name, DOB, address, Aadhaar, etc.).
column4: Ensure the **permanent address** matches your domicile certificate.

column3: In the “Apply for Scholarship” section, locate the **Devnarayan Post‑Matric** scheme and click **“Apply”.**
column4: The scheme code for 2026‑27 is **DM‑PM‑2026** (displayed on the portal).

column3: Upload scanned copies (PDF/JPEG, max 2 MB each).
Enter your **course details**, **institution name**, **year of study**, **previous exam marks**, and **family income**.
column4: Double‑check the **course code** and **institution code** (available on the portal).

column3: Review all entries, click **“Submit”.** You will receive an **Application ID** (e.g., DMPM‑2026‑001234).
column4: Save this ID – you’ll need it for future queries and for uploading any additional documents.

column3: The cell will verify your documents (usually within 7‑10 working days).
column4: You may be called for **in‑person verification** at the District Education Office if required.

column3: Once approved, you’ll receive an **award letter** (PDF) and a **bank account verification** form.
column4: Fill the bank form, sign, and upload a **cancelled cheque** or **bank passbook page**.

column3: After bank verification, the amount is transferred to the provided account.
column4: Keep the **transaction receipt** for future reference.

column3: For the next academic year, repeat steps **1‑9** before the renewal deadline (usually 30 days before the start of the new session).
column4: Use the same Application ID with “Renewal” option.

### 5️⃣ Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs)

column3: **Answer**

column2: **Can I apply if I am studying outside Rajasthan?**
column3: **No.** The scholarship is only for students **studying in Rajasthan** (government, aided, or recognized private institutions).

column2: **What if my family income is slightly above ₹ 4 lakhs?**
column3: You will be **ineligible** for this particular scheme. However, you may explore **central scholarships** (e.g., *National Scholarship Portal* for SC/ST/OBC) that have higher income ceilings.
No. The amount is **exempt from income tax** under Section 10(16) of the Income Tax Act, as it is a government‑provided scholarship for education.

column2: **Can I receive this scholarship along with a central OBC scholarship?**
column3: **Yes**, provided the total amount does **not exceed** the permissible limit set by the state (₹ 25,000) and you are not a **full‑time** recipient of another post‑matric scholarship.

column2: **What if I change my course or institution mid‑year?**
column3: You must **inform the Rajasthan Scholarship Cell** within 15 days and submit the new admission letter. The scholarship may be **re‑evaluated** and could be discontinued if the new course is not covered under the scheme.
Typically **7‑10 working days** after submission. If additional verification is needed, you may be called for an in‑person interview, extending the timeline by another 5‑7 days.

column2: **What if I miss the 28 Sept deadline?**
column3: Applications submitted after the deadline are **rejected**. You will have to wait for the **next admission cycle** (usually the following academic year).
Yes. You can raise a complaint on the portal under **“Grievance/Help Desk”** or contact the **State Scholarship Cell** at **0141‑252‑XXXX** (Rajasthan).

- **If you are applying for a technical **degree** (B.Tech, B.Arch, B.Pharm, etc.)** – the relevant deadline is **13 Sept 2026** (first row).
- **If you are applying under the broader AICTE Pragati Scheme (which may also cover diploma courses and allows two sisters per family)** – the deadline is **23 Sept 2026** (second row).
- **If you are enrolled in a technical **diploma** (e.g., Diploma in Engineering, Diploma in Pharmacy, etc.)** – the deadline is also **13 Sept 2026** (third row).
### Quick Checklist for a Smooth Application
1. **Confirm Eligibility**
- Indian citizen, female.
- Enrolled in an **AICTE‑approved** technical degree or diploma programme for the current academic year.
- For the “AICTE Pragati Scholarship Scheme for Girl Students” – a maximum of **two girl children per family** can receive the award.
2. **Gather Required Documents**
- **Proof of admission** (admission letter/offer letter from the institute).
- **Academic transcripts** of the previous qualifying exam.
- **Income certificate** of the family (if required for the specific scheme).
- **Identity proof** (Aadhaar card, PAN card, or passport).
- **Passport‑size photograph** (recent, with white background).
- **Bank account details** (passbook or cancelled cheque) for scholarship disbursement.
3. **Application Procedure (common steps)**
- Visit the **AICTE Pragati Scholarship portal** (usually hosted on the AICTE website or the Ministry of Education’s scholarship portal).
- Register using your **email/mobile number** and create a password.
- Fill in personal, academic, and family‑income details.
- Upload the scanned copies of the required documents (PDF/JPEG, size ≤ 200 KB each).
- Review the application, submit, and note down the **application reference number**.
- You will receive an **acknowledgement email/SMS** with further instructions (e.g., verification, interview, or document verification).
4. **After Submission**
- Keep a copy of the **acknowledgement receipt**.
- Monitor your email/SMS for any **additional document requests**.
- The selection committee usually releases the **short‑list** within 2–3 weeks after the deadline.
- Successful candidates receive the **award letter** and details for bank‑transfer of the scholarship amount.
### Helpful Links (as of August 2026)
- **AICTE Pragati Scholarship Portal:** `https://scholarship.aicte-india.org/pragati`
- **Official AICTE Guidelines (PDF):** `https://aicte-india.org/scholarships/Pragati_Scholarship_Guidelines_2026.pdf`

- Email: `pragati.scholarship@aicte-india.org`
**Bottom line:**
- **13 Sept 2026** for technical **degree** and **diploma** scholarships.
- **23 Sept 2026** for the broader AICTE Pragati Scheme (covers both degree & diploma, with the “two‑girls‑per‑family” rule).

Make sure you submit **well before** the respective deadline to avoid any last‑minute technical glitches. column1: **No – as of August 2026 there is no centrally‑run scholarship or award officially titled “PM Modi Student Excellence Award” in the Government‑of‑India scholarship catalogue.**

The name sometimes appears in media or on private‑sector websites, but it is **not** a recognized scheme of the Ministry of Education, Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment, or any other central ministry that publishes the official scholarship list (e.g., PM‑YASASVI, National Means‑Cum‑Merit, Rajiv Gandhi National Fellowship, etc.).

column3: What it actually refers to

column2: **Press releases / news articles** that mention “PM Modi” together with “student excellence”
column3: Usually they are talking about **existing** schemes (e.g., PM‑YASASVI, National Means‑Cum‑Merit) that the Prime Minister has inaugurated, not a separate award.

column2: **State‑level or private‑sector programmes** that use “PM Modi” in the title for branding
column3: Some NGOs, corporate CSR initiatives, or state governments may name a **local** scholarship “PM Modi Student Excellence Award” to honour the Prime Minister’s vision. These are **not** part of the central‑government list and their eligibility, amount, and deadlines vary widely.
Could be a shorthand for **“Prime Minister’s”** scholarship, such as **PM‑YASASVI** (Prime Minister – Yashasvi) or **PM‑KVY** (Prime Minister’s Knowledge‑Vikas Yojana).

column1: ## What you can do next
1. **Check the official portals**
- **National Scholarship Portal (NSP)** – https://scholarships.gov.in
- **Ministry of Education – Scholarship Section** – https://www.education.gov.in/scholarships
- **State‑wise scholarship portals** (e.g., Maharashtra’s “Maharashtra Scholarship Portal”, Tamil Nadu’s “Scholarship Management System”).
Use the search box and type **“Modi”**, **“Excellence”**, or **“Award”**. If a scheme exists, it will appear with a dedicated application link.
2. **If you heard about it from a school/college**
- Ask the institution’s **Scholarship/Student‑Affairs Office** for the official notification (PDF, Gazette, or Ministry order).
- Request the **application form** and a copy of the **eligibility criteria**.
3. **If it is a private/CSR initiative**
- Verify the **organising body** (e.g., a corporate foundation, a state government department, or an NGO).
- Look for:
- **Eligibility** (category, class/grade, income limit)
- **Award amount** (one‑time, per‑semester, or monthly)
- **Application deadline**
- **Required documents** (marksheets, income certificate, recommendation letters, etc.)

1. **Identify which scheme(s) match your profile** (caste/community, income, academic performance, level of study).
2. **Gather the required documents** *before* you start the online application – this saves time and avoids re‑uploads.
3. **Create an Aadhar‑linked bank account** (if you don’t already have one). Most scholarships disburse directly to this account.
4. **Mark the deadlines** on your calendar (especially the two that close in October).
5. **Apply early** – many scholarships require verification of college admission, which may take a few weeks after you receive your admission letter.

column3: Answer

column2: **Can I apply for more than one scholarship at the same time?**
column3: **Yes.** Most schemes are **cumulative** unless they specifically state “only one scholarship per student.” For example, you can receive the **Rajarshi Shahu** state scholarship **and** the **Central Sector** scholarship together, because they are funded by different authorities.

Some schemes (e.g., **Rajarshi Shahu**) have a strict deadline. If you miss it, you must wait for the **next academic year**. Others (e.g., **Post‑Matric SC**) accept **late applications** until the **verification window** closes, but the chance of approval may reduce.

column2: **Do I need a separate bank account for each scholarship?**
column3: **No.** One **Aadhar‑linked** bank account can receive multiple scholarship credits. Ensure the **account name matches your name** exactly as on your Aadhar.

column2: **I am a Maharashtra resident but studying outside the state (e.g., Delhi). Can I still get the Rajarshi Shahu scholarship?**
column3: **No.** The Rajarshi Shahu scholarship is **restricted to students studying in Maharashtra** institutions. However, you can still apply for **central schemes** (Post‑Matric SC, Central Sector, etc.).

column2: **My family income is just above the limit (₹4.2 Lakhs). Can I still apply?**
column3: For the **Rajarshi Shahu** scholarship, the limit is **strict**; you would be **ineligible**. Look for **national schemes** that have a higher income ceiling (e.g., **Post‑Matric SC** often allows up to **₹6 Lakhs**).

column2: **I have a disability (80 %). Are there additional scholarships?**
column3: Yes. The **National Scholarship for Persons with Disabilities (NSP‑PWD)** offers **₹40,000–₹80,000** per year. Apply via **NSP** under the “**Scholarship for Differently‑Abled**” category.

column2: **How long does the verification process take?**
column3: Typically **15‑30 days** after submission, but it can extend to **45 days** during peak periods (July‑Sept). You can track status on the portal; any delays are usually communicated via SMS/Email.

column2: **What if I change my course or college after receiving the scholarship?**
column3: You must **inform the scholarship authority** within **15 days** of the change and upload the new admission proof. Failure to do so may lead to **suspension** of the scholarship.

column2: **Do I need to submit a yearly progress report?**
column3: Most scholarships require an **annual academic progress report** (marksheet/grade card) to continue receiving funds. Upload it on the portal before the **next disbursement cycle**.
**No.** All the listed scholarships are **free of charge**. Beware of any third‑party agencies asking for money; apply directly through the official portals.

column2: **Do I need to submit income proof for the Central Sector Scheme?**
column3: **No.** The scheme is purely merit‑based; only a **class‑12 mark sheet** (showing percentile) and **admission proof** are required.

column2: **What if my family income rises to > ₹6 L after I get the scholarship?**
column3: For merit‑only schemes (Central Sector, INSPIRE, university scholarships) **no income re‑verification** is needed. For means‑based schemes you would have to report the change, and the scholarship may be discontinued.

column2: **Can I apply for multiple scholarships simultaneously?**
column3: **Yes.** There is no restriction on applying for more than one scholarship, provided you meet each scheme’s eligibility. However, you cannot receive **duplicate funding for the same expense** (e.g., two scholarships covering the same tuition).

column2: **What if I miss the 8 Oct deadline?**
column3: The Central Scheme’s portal **closes** on that date. You would need to wait for the **next academic year** (usually announced in July‑August). Meanwhile, explore other merit‑based scholarships that have later deadlines.

column2: **I am from a state other than Odisha – can I still get the Mathematics scholarship?**
column3: No. The **Transfer Financial Assistance – Mathematics Scholarship** is **state‑specific** to Odisha. Look for your own state’s **subject‑specific** scholarships (e.g., Karnataka’s “Science & Mathematics Scholarship”).

column2: **Do I need a separate PAN for the scholarship?**
column3: Not mandatory for the Central Scheme, but having a PAN **speeds up verification** and is required for any **tax‑exempt** scholarship amount > ₹10,000.
